what: The heuristic precomputes the CVRP structure once in new(): propositional loc/visited facts for all objects, numeric ids for load() and vehicles(), best-effort capacity/max_vehicles/demand values, direct and via-depot travel-cost matrices extracted primarily from grounded visit and visit-via-depot operators, return-to-depot costs, and sorted nearest-neighbor lists for direct and via-depot moves. In compute_heuristic it reads the current location, load, vehicles, and visited set. If a goal state is detected it returns 0. If all customers are visited but the vehicle is not at the depot it returns the return-to-depot cost. If remaining demand exceeds residual plus remaining fleet capacity it returns a large finite dead-end penalty. Otherwise it runs a small greedy capacitated completion simulation that respects direct visit capacity feasibility and visit-via-depot vehicle availability, adding a small resource-pressure term based on estimated extra routes. The final heuristic value is h_route + h_capacity.
why: The representative instances are fleet-limited capacitated routing problems with an explicit metric travel-cost matrix. A useful heuristic must distinguish states by current location, load, vehicles used, and which customers remain. Unvisited-count and simple depot-distance sums ignore vehicle reloads and load constraints. This design uses grounded operator costs to recover the true metric costs of direct visit and visit-via-depot transitions, and then simulates a greedy completion that must respect capacity and fleet limits. The resource infeasibility check handles dead-end states where remaining demand cannot fit. The final return-to-depot cost is added when all customers are served but the vehicle is still away. Precomputed sorted adjacency lists keep per-state evaluation cheap while making the estimate considerably more informed than pure geometric or count baselines.
design: Operator-based travel cost reconstruction from grounded visit and visit-via-depot actions
Capacity/resource lower bound and dead-end detection
complexity: O(n^2) worst-case per state due to scanning sorted neighbor lists during the small greedy completion, though with tens of customers and pre-sorted lists it is very fast. Static construction is O(total facts + grounded operators + n^2 log n).
fallbacks: If some direct travel-cost arcs are missing after operator extraction, the code attempts a fallback scan of numeric variables whose exact names start with PNE travel-cost( or travel-cost(. Missing via-depot arcs are conservatively filled as return_cost[from] + depot_to[to] when both legs are known. If no depot outbound cost can be reconstructed, construction fails with a clear error. If capacity, max_vehicles, or demand variables are absent by exact-name lookup, permissive defaults are used: INF for capacity/max_vehicles and 0.0 for demand, so the heuristic still runs without aborting.
known_limitations: The greedy completion is not optimal; it may over- or under-estimate because it commits to the nearest currently feasible direct or via-depot move without considering future route consequences.
The resource-pressure term is a small hand-tuned penalty and may slightly overcount costs already present in the simulated route.
If the PDDL translator folds capacity/demand variables into derived expressions, the resource infeasibility check degrades to permissive defaults and may miss some dead ends.
